issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for the bitmap pixel buffer: in the template repository the Bitmap24 class declares the member 'data' as 'int *data' (Bitmap24.hpp) but the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) allocates and uses it as a char array (new char[...], indexed and assigned with char values). The solution repository uses 'char *data' in the header (matching the implementation). This mismatch in the template will cause compilation/type errors (assigning char* to int* and incompatible indexing/assignments) and will confuse or block students working from the template.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the member declaration in the template header to match the implementation and the solution: replace 'int *data;' with 'char *data;' (or use 'unsigned char *' if you prefer explicitly unsigned pixel bytes). Update the comment to note 3 bytes per pixel. This preserves the pedagogical intent while fixing the compilation/type error.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 class's 'data' field is declared with a different type in the template header than in the example implementation and in the solution header. In template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp the member is declared as 'int *data;' but the implementation (template/example/src/Bitmap24.cpp) allocates and treats 'data' as a byte buffer (new char[...]) and the solution header declares the member as 'char *data;'. This mismatch makes it unclear which type students should use and will cause compilation/type errors when building the provided template (violating the 'must compile' requirement).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Bitmap24::data member declaration consistent with the implementation and solution by changing the template header declaration to 'char *data;'. This aligns the conceptual entity (the image byte buffer) across template and solution and prevents compilation/type errors. (If a different representation is intended, update both the implementation and solution consistently and document the choice in the problem/template.)
